newsitem.title: USA: State may address Lilco, LIPA plan on Weds.
newsitem.headline: State may address Lilco, LIPA plan on Weds.

text.p: The proposed partial takeover of Long Island Lighting Co by the Long Island Power Authority may come up for state approval on Wednesday, LIPA said.

The New York State Division of Budget on Monday confirmed the Public Authorities Control Board will meet on Wednesday at the State Capitol in Albany. The board must be unanimous in its support of the transaction for the deal to proceed.
LIPA spokesman Seth Hulkower also confirmed the meeting but said there is no guarantee the takeover will be discussed. A formal agenda from the PACB was not available on Monday.

The PACB is a three-member panel comprised of Governor George Pataki (R), Senate Majority Leader Joseph Bruno (R) and State Assembly Speaker Sheldon Silver (D). Silver last month questioned the wisdom of the $7.3 billion tax-exempt bond sale that would be necessary to pay for the acquisition, suggesting that it may be excessive and that it only benefits one area of the state.

Key elements of the plan are a LIPA takeover of Lilco's electric transmission and distribution system, most regulatory assets and its share of Nine Mile Point 2 nuclear power plant. The takeover would be paid for through a stock purchase from a Brooklyn Union Gas /Lilco holding company, financed, in part, by the proposed bond sale.
The meeting will take place at 1400 EDT/1800 GMT in room 123 of the State Capitol in Albany.

The proposal must also garner approval from the New York State Public Service Commission, the Federal Energy Regulatory Commission, the Nuclear Regulatory Commission and the Securities and Exchange Commission.
